about: Polar lab (docs/apcalcbc-spec.md section 6; builder T2). The curves and every number live in calculus-bc/assets/tools/math/polar-lab.js; contexts unlock with their Unit 9 topics. Checked by scripts/lib/apcalcbc-tool-checks/polar-lab.mjs.
intro: A polar curve $r = f(\theta)$ drawn as $\theta$ sweeps, with the area swept so far shaded and the setup $\frac{1}{2}\int r^2\,d\theta$ built beside it. Press Play or drag around the curve. The graph of $r$ against $\theta$ shows when the point moves toward or away from the origin; with two curves, the region between them is swept the same way.
howItWorksTitle: How the curves and areas are computed
howItWorks:
• Points: $x = r\cos\theta$ and $y = r\sin\theta$. Where $r < 0$ the point is plotted on the opposite ray, at distance $|r|$ from the origin.
  • Toward or away: the distance from the origin is $|r|$, so the point moves away when $r$ and $\frac{dr}{d\theta}$ have the same sign and toward when their signs differ.
  • Slope: $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}$ with $\frac{dy}{d\theta} = \frac{dr}{d\theta}\sin\theta + r\cos\theta$ and $\frac{dx}{d\theta} = \frac{dr}{d\theta}\cos\theta - r\sin\theta$ (the product rule on each).
  • Area: a thin slice is a sector of area $\frac{1}{2}r^2\,\Delta\theta$, so the area swept from $\alpha$ to $\beta$ is $\frac{1}{2}\int_\alpha^\beta r^2\,d\theta$. Between two curves, $\frac{1}{2}\int_\alpha^\beta (R^2 - r^2)\,d\theta$, outer $R$ minus inner $r$, with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ where they meet. Values are integrated numerically (adaptive Simpson).
  • A sweep that traces part of the curve twice counts that area twice: one petal or loop runs between consecutive zeros of $r$.
